title: Wall Street Rebound Tests Resistance as Crypto Liquidity Contracts
description:
A comprehensive weekly recap of global markets for the week ending November 28, 2026.
Stocks stage a sharp Thanksgiving comeback while tech megacaps face heavy structural hurdles.
Bitcoin consolidates below critical resistance as DeFi liquidity faces severe protocol stress.
Sources: Jeremy Lefebvre, Michael Pizzino, Jason Pizzino, Marco Casario, 0xTalks, MindTheChart.

segments.heading: Wall Street Thanksgiving Reversal
segments.narration: Wall Street staged its strongest Thanksgiving rebound in over a year, lifting the S&P 500 out of correction territory. Yet severe structural hurdles remain. In this weekly recap, we examine the volatile semiconductor turnaround, the multi-month gold liquidation, and mounting liquidity pressure across crypto.

segments.heading: Weekly Market Snapshot
segments.narration: Equities rebounded aggressively this week as panic selling subsided. The S&P 500 rose 1.7% over the past five days to 7,297, gaining 1.6% in Friday's session. The Dow Jones led major benchmarks with a 3.4% weekly surge to 50,775, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.1% to 24,130. Volatility cooled dramatically, with the VIX dropping nearly 34% across the week to settle at 24. Bond markets showed mild stabilization as the US 10-year Treasury yield held at 4.9%. In commodities and digital assets, Gold rebounded on Friday to $3,640 but remains down 1.3% over the week. Bitcoin trades near $59,673, down 2.4% over five days.

segments.heading: Wall Street Tests Breakdown Levels
segments.narration: The Thanksgiving holiday week delivered a massive relief rally, but the underlying technical landscape demands careful verification. The S&P 500 gapped up from its recent lows, closing right at the lower boundary of its critical breakdown zone between 7,250 and 7,350. A decisive consolidation above 7,300 is required to establish an interim bottom and prevent a retest of the November 20 low. While the Dow Jones managed to test its February highs near 51,500, the tech-heavy Nasdaq remains visibly weaker. Trading below its 50% retracement level at 27,300, the index is down over 20% from its cycle peak and needs to reclaim 28,000 to confirm a trend reversal. Market internals reveal conflicting dynamics. Retail investor sentiment dropped to extreme fear, with bearish sentiment climbing to 51.4%, nearly 20 points above historical norms. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 forward price-to-earnings ratio sits near 18.3, pointing toward fair valuation rather than outright bubble pricing. However, four consecutive positive annual returns for major indexes keep the probability of a future corrective year elevated. Without follow-through volume above structural resistance, this bounce behaves primarily as a short squeeze inside an unfinished correction.

segments.heading: Semiconductor Volatility and Margins
segments.narration: Semiconductors dominated trading volatility throughout the week. Nvidia shares rebounded over 30% from their intraday trough following leadership stability, but the stock has experienced single-day swings of 5% or more five separate times in November. From its October peak, Nvidia suffered a 48% drawdown before bouncing. Net profit margins near 60% face mounting pressure as competition intensifies and hyperscalers evaluate massive artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Tech giants are projected to deploy nearly $800 billion in capital expenditures, raising scrutiny over return on invested capital. Simultaneously, Advanced Micro Devices has demonstrated superior relative performance against Nvidia over recent multi-month periods. Projections pointing toward 2030 data center revenues closing the competitive gap have attracted institutional capital, with long-term revenue estimates spanning $160 billion to $195 billion. Historical fractal comparisons to 2018 suggest that semiconductor rallies during corrective phases often encounter sharp tax-loss harvesting pressure. With underperforming mega-caps facing institutional portfolio rebalancing through the first three weeks of December, chip valuations remain exposed to fresh downside tests before durable accumulation takes place.
bullets: AMD relative performance strengthens in chips

segments.heading: Historic Unwind in Precious Metals
segments.narration: Gold and silver have endured one of their sharpest unwinds in decades, breaking traditional safe-haven expectations during recent equity pullbacks. Gold futures dropped nearly 39% from their peak over a 10-month stretch, trading near $3,640 per ounce. This correction stems from forced global liquidations rather than an abandonment of hard assets. As equity margins collapsed earlier in the month, institutional traders dumped liquid commodity positions to cover collateral calls. The structural divergence in gold remains historic: paper derivative trading volume now exceeds physical vault transactions by roughly 165 times. While paper contracts faced heavy dumping and exchange-traded fund outflows from North American accounts, physical demand stayed exceptionally robust. Central banks purchased 321 tonnes in the third quarter alone, with reserve accumulation continuing steadily. Technically, gold trades just above its 50% retracement level. A sustained recovery requires clearing overhead resistance at $3,900, while a long-term bullish continuation demands monthly closes back above $4,500. Until forced deleveraging subsides and the US dollar index weakens from the 103 to 105 range, precious metals remain locked in a multi-year consolidation structure.

segments.heading: Bitcoin Cycle Meets Resistance
segments.narration: Digital assets continue to lag broader equities, failing to mount an equivalent holiday comeback. Bitcoin closed the week at $59,673, maintaining a multi-day decline and trading well below its 200-day exponential moving average. The current bear market structure has now persisted for 411 days from its previous peak, matching historical cycle durations almost to the day. On the weekly timeframe, Bitcoin has carved out an expanding megaphone pattern. The lower boundary of this formation rests between $58,000 and $59,000, which has served as immediate structural support. However, the price lacks three consecutive daily gains, keeping the dominant trend downward. Overhead resistance is established at $62,000, with the critical macro pivot sitting at $67,000. Reclaiming $67,000 is necessary to confirm a genuine trend reversal. If the $58,000 support gives way under renewed dollar strength, the technical projection points toward downside liquidity pockets between $52,000 and $49,000. Relief rallies in prolonged bear cycles historically take twice as long to develop as the drops that preceded them, indicating that short-term volatility will persist before a cycle bottom forms.

segments.heading: DeFi Strain and Stablecoin Drops
segments.narration: Liquidity conditions across decentralized finance experienced acute stress this week, led by an unwinding in the Sky protocol, formerly MakerDAO. The crisis exposed structural vulnerabilities around concentrated leverage, where founder-led borrowing reached $77 million backed by platform governance tokens. A run on the peg stability module occurred when a single entity converted 1.49 billion USDS into USDC within a nine-minute span. Borrowing utilization on integrated lending markets like Morpho spiked to 99.3%, freezing secondary liquidity and triggering cascading collateral redemptions. This individual protocol shock highlights a wider contraction in crypto liquidity. Total stablecoin supply has decreased by approximately $20 billion since October, falling from $300 billion to $280 billion. When stablecoins exit the ecosystem, market depth dries up, exacerbating price slippage across both major and alternative tokens. Until central bank interest rates fall sufficiently to encourage risk-on stablecoin minting, decentralized finance valuations will reflect persistent liquidity constraints. Risk management requires tracking total collateral concentration rather than relying on nominal token market caps.

segments.heading: Defensive Inflows and Risk Gauges
segments.narration: The divergence between speculative tech and defensive equities widened significantly across global markets. Quantitative indicators tracked a sharp shift in the macro regime, with risk appetite metrics plummeting from neutral readings of 50 in October to extreme risk-off levels of 20 this week. Sector performance clearly reflected this rotation. Consumer Staples and Utilities led institutional inflows, while Information Technology dropped to the bottom tier of multi-factor performance models. Over the past month, large-cap chip designers such as Marvell Technology dropped 44%, illustrating the penalty imposed on stretched valuations. These conditions underscore the value of mechanical portfolio hedging. Options overlays such as long-dated put protection and cash reserves have successfully dampened drawdowns during recent volatility spikes. The asymmetry of market loss is unforgiving: a 56% decline requires a 130% recovery just to break even. Maintaining disciplined asset allocations, setting aside dedicated capital for deep corrections, and avoiding premature dip buying in high-beta names represent the defining strategies of this cycle transition.

Tech sector ranks lowest in quant models

segments.heading: Crucial US Employment Data Ahead
segments.narration: The coming week brings a dense calendar of macroeconomic reports capable of setting December interest rate expectations. On Tuesday, December 1, ISM Manufacturing data will provide the latest reading on industrial activity. Wednesday follows with the ADP private employment survey. On Thursday, ISM Services data will gauge health across the domestic consumer sector. The week culminates on Friday, December 4, with the comprehensive US employment report, where nonfarm payroll figures and unemployment data will be released at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. With interest rate markets leaning heavily toward tight Federal Reserve policy and year-end tax-loss harvesting approaching, these macro data points will determine whether this week's equity bounce can overcome overhead resistance.

segments.heading: Budget Carrier Enters Bankruptcy
segments.narration: In European corporate news, long-haul budget carrier Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy this week after failing to secure vital emergency funding. The airline succumbed to the dual pressures of soaring jet fuel expenses and fierce transatlantic competition. Despite attempts to restructure debt and negotiate credit facilities, mounting operational costs depleted cash reserves. The insolvency filing delivers an abrupt halt to the carrier's operations, underscoring how persistent energy inflation and tight financing conditions continue to claim corporate victims across fuel-intensive industries.
bullets: Surging jet fuel costs drain cash
